title: Impact Assessment of Repeated Exposure of Organotypic 3D Bronchial and Nasal Tissue Culture Models to Whole Cigarette Smoke
protocol: Handle reconstituted tissue models under sterile conditions.
Add 0.7 ml of pre-warmed (37°C) assay medium to each well of a new sterile 24-well plate.
Transfer the tissue culture inserts from sterile packaging into the prepared 24-well plate containing assay medium.
Maintain tissues in an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 and 90% humidity.
Replace the medium every two days.
Examine the tissues under a light microscope during each medium change to check for contamination and leakage.
Three days prior to exposure experiments, wash the apical side of the tissue culture with 200 µl of culture medium.
Pre-warm the climatic chamber of the in vitro exposure system and the cultivation base module to 37°C.
Fill the cultivation base module with 17.5 ml of medium per row.
Remove tissues from the incubator and place them under the hood.
Transfer tissue culture inserts from the culture plate to the cultivation base module of the in vitro exposure system.
Cover the cultivation base module with a glass lid.
Transfer the tissues in the climatic chamber of the in vitro exposure system for exposure to mainstream CS.
If the in vitro exposure system is equipped with a microbalance, set up the Quartz crystal microbalance before running the exposure.
Replace the crystals in the microbalance modules connected to each row of the dilution/distribution system.
Connect the microbalance module to the microbalance software.
Set the scale of the measurement to zero in the software.
Expose the tissues according to the experimental procedure.
Generate cigarette smoke using a 30-port carousel smoking machine according to the Health Canada Intense regime.
Dilute mainstream CS to 16% vol/vol if necessary for toxicity considerations.
Use 60% humidified-air for control samples (air-exposed).
Expose tissues for 6-7 min in the in vitro exposure system.
Place exposed tissues back in the incubator at 37 °C (5% CO2, 90% humidity) for 1 hr.
Repeat steps of exposure and recovery three more times.
Transfer back the tissues from the cultivation base module to the culture plate after exposure experiment completion.
Record ciliary beating prior to the exposure and directly after the exposure as per experimental plan.
Remove tissue culture plates from the incubator and leave them under the hood at room temperature for 30 min to stabilize cilia beating.
Place tissues under the light microscope connected to CiliaMetrix Software.
Record movie and frequency (in Hertz) of ciliary beating every 3 sec for 1 minute.
Return the tissues back to the incubator at 37 °C (5% CO2, 90% humidity).
Measure TEER 3 days before and 48 hours after exposure under sterile conditions using Chopstick Electrode connected to a voltohmmeter.
Add 200 μl of culture media to the apical surface of human bronchial tissues.
Turn on the EVOMX machine; wash the electrode with a 70% ethanol solution.
Wash the electrode with the culture medium.
Measure resistance by inserting the electrode into the medium on the apical side of the tissue culture without touching the tissue.
Repeat measurement five times to obtain quintuplicate measurements.
Gently remove the medium from the apical side of the tissue cultures using an aspirator.
Return the tissue cultures to the incubator at 37 °C (5% CO2, 90% humidity) for culturing.

Prepare luciferin detection reagent by transferring the entire contents of the bottle of the appropriate reconstitution buffer to the amber bottle containing the luciferin detection reagent according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Store aliquots of 2 ml at -20 °C for a maximum of 1 month.
Warm Luciferin detection reagent to room temperature.
Incubate tissue inserts for 48 hours following CS exposure at 37 °C.
Incubate tissue inserts for 3 hr or overnight with the Luciferin-CEE substrate diluted at 1:50 in basal culture medium.
Transfer 50 µl of culture medium from each tissue insert to a 96-well opaque white luminometer plate at RT.
Add 50 µl of luciferin detection reagent to each well to initiate a luminescent reaction.
Incubate the plate at RT for 20 min.
Read the luminescence using a luminometer.
Prepare a box with dry ice.
Prepare an amount of blades (one per 3D insert).
Prepare cold PBS without calcium chloride and magnesium chloride.
Prepare one 25 ml glass pipet.
Turn on aspiration machine.
Collect the plate of the 3D organotypic tissue inserts from the incubator.
Wash each insert on the plate 3 times with cold PBS.
Aspirate PBS with a glass needle between washes.
After the third wash, aspirate with PBS and cover the plate to prevent drying of the insert.
Cut out the insert membrane until it lies flat down on the blade for each insert from the plate.
Transfer the tissue (along with the insert membrane) from the blade to the homogenizing tube appropriately labelled.
Screw the lid on the tube containing the tissue sample.
Shake and vortex the tube.
Freeze the sample in dry ice and store at -80 °C or continue to extract RNA.
Label all tubes and columns according to the randomization design if applicable.
Take out samples from -80°C freezer and thaw them on ice until completely defrosted.
Grind samples with homogenizing instrument on 6000 Hz for 45 sec.
Repeat grinding if the samples are not properly homogenized, then leave samples for 5 min at room temperature.
Add 140 μl chloroform to the sample and vortex for 10-15 sec.
Transfer the supernatant from the homogenizing tube to a Phase lock tube and shake on a thermoshaker for 2 min at 1400 rpm and room temperature.
Incubate samples for 2 min at room temperature and centrifuge samples at 12,000 x g for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase in a new 2 ml tube.
Load all necessary reagents in the extraction robot according to the manufacturer protocol sheet.
Select the appropriate protocol and set the elution volume (30 μl).
Run the extraction robot.
Remove rotor adapters when the run is finished.
Keep elution tubes immediately at 4°C for further analysis or at -80°C for long term storage.
Determine the quantity of the isolated RNA using an UV reader according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Check the quality and integrity of RNA using microfluidic-gel-based lab-on-a-chip and an UV reader according to manufacturer instructions.
Randomize samples to avoid batch effects for Affymetrix GeneChip High throughput 3’IVT Express Kit analysis.
Prepare target synthesis starting from 100 ng of total RNA in 3 µl RNAse-free water with a 16 h incubation time.
Start the RNA amplification process.
Prepare Poly-A RNA spike-in control solution by serial dilution:
Mix 2 µl polyA control stock with 36 µl dilution buffer for dilution 1.
Mix 2 µl of dilution 1 with 98 µl of dilution buffer for dilution 2.
Mix 4 µl of dilution 2 with 196 µl of dilution buffer for dilution 3.
Mix 20 µl of dilution 3 with 180 µl of dilution buffer for dilution 4.
Dilute the RNA in RNAse free water to achieve a concentration of 33.3 ng/µl.
Add 2 μl of polyA control solution to 3 μl of total RNA sample directly in a 96 well plate.
Prepare the liquid handling system and target synthesis.
Place the plates on the robot.
Place all required reagents and labware on the deck.
Start the procedure by preparing appropriate mastermixes.
Incubate samples in the automated remote controlled PCR block.
Perform quality control check of amplification process.
If aRNA quality is acceptable, add 8 μl of fragmentation 5X buffer to each sample.
Otherwise, repeat previous steps starting from RNA preparation.
Use fragmented aRNA immediately or store undiluted and fragmented aRNA at -20°C (or -70°C for long-term storage).
Perform second quality control analysis by picking up randomly 12 samples in the plate.
Transfer 1 μl of each sample to microfluidics gel-based system for fragmentation efficiency check.
Scan chip barcodes.
Register each sample in manufacturer’s software according to instructions.
Mix 4.2 µl of control oligonucleotide B2 (3nM).
Add 12.5 µl of 20x eukaryotic hybridization controls.
Combine 25 µl of 100% DMSO.
Include 125 µl of 2x hybridization buffer.
Add 50 µl of H2O to achieve a final volume of 216.7 µl.
Hybridize positive and negative controls before processing samples.
Pre-wet the array with 200 µl of pre-hybridization mix.
Place the chip in the hybridization oven at 45 °C and 60 RPM for 10 min.
Denature the plate containing the final cocktail hybridization mix in a PCR block at 99 °C for 5 min, then at 45 °C for 5 min.
Remove pre-hybridization mix from the array.
Replace with 200 µl of the hybridization cocktail target (one sample per chip).
Place the array into the hybridization oven set at 45 °C for 16 hr with a rotation speed of 60 RPM.
Run "Fluidics" from the software menu bar.
Select the module of interest and Prime_450 program to all modules.
Place tubing for Wash Buffer A in a bottle (400 ml).
Place tubing for Wash Buffer B in a bottle (200 ml).
Place tubing for milliQ Water in a bottle (500 ml).
Lift up the needles and place 600 μl stain cocktail 1 at position #1.
Place 600 μl stain cocktail 2 at position #2.
Place 900 μl Array Holding buffer solution at position #3.
Aspirate the cocktail from the chip after O/N incubation in the oven.
Fill the microarray with 250 μl Wash Buffer A.
Assign the right chip to each module and select the FS450-001 protocol.
Run each module following instructions on screen for 90 minutes.
Remove the chip once the LCD screen indicates “Eject Cartridge” message.
Inspect if there are any bubbles in the chip.
If bubbles are present, fill the array entirely with the Array holding buffer.
Apply stickers onto the septa to avoid leaks in the scanner.
Clean the microarray window prior to loading it into the Scanner.
Warm up the scanner before use.
Load the chip into the autoloader of the scanner and start scanning.
Check the image generated after approximately 12 minutes per chip.
Align the grid (if necessary) to identify probe cells.
Open an R session and load the affy, gcrma, and affyPLM packages.
Read raw data files using the command: data.affybatch<-ReadAffy("path to the folder where are stored the CEL files").
Subtract background correction and perform quantile normalization to generate probe set expression values using the gcrma package with the command: eset.norm<-gcrma(data.affybatch).
Generate RNA degradation plots with the command: deg<-AffyRNAdeg(data.affybatch).
Extract the coefficient of the RNA degradation slope running the command: slope=deg$slope.
Plot the slope coefficient and identify possible outliers.
Generate NUSE and RLE plots by running these commands: Pset<-fitPLM(data.affybatch), RLE(Pset), and NUSE(Pset).
Identify if some of the boxplots generated are outliers based on the criteria provided for deg$slope, NUSE plot, and RLE plot metrics.
Fit an overall linear model to the data for specific contrasts of interest.
Generate raw P values for each probe set on the microarray.
Adjust raw P values using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure from the Limma package.
Select a probeset per gene as representative of the gene for further analyses.
Compute (log2-) fold changes for each gene under the network.
Compute the signed Laplacian matrix L of the network.
Calculate scores for the backbone by f=L3-1L2Tx.
Compute the signed Laplacian, Q, of the network with all edge signs reversed.
Compute the NPA score using the formula NPA=fTQf.
Calculate the confidence interval for the NPA scores.
Compute the backbone edge permutation p-value.
Compute the transcript layer permutation p-value.
Identify leading nodes that contribute up to 80% of the NPA score.
